subject: Peak window latency spike — coordination, product asks, and customer-facing draft
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Aug 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [SEV-Low] P95 jump in peak routing window (08:05–08:20 PT)

Hey team,

We saw a ~2.4x jump in P95 latency for gen-api endpoints serving BrightCart during the 08:05–08:20 PT window. Error rate did not increase materially, CPU/GPU utilization remained within normal bands, but GPU tail latencies on a subset of instances (gpu-pool-12c) spiked.

What we've collected so far:
- Traces: sampling shows long scheduling wait times on 3 nodes (see attached profile_dump_230823.txt).
- Repro: synthetic load against the same routing policy reproduces a smaller P95 increase (x1.3) locally.
- Cache: KV hit rate steady; not a mass cache miss event.

Immediate asks:
1) SRE: can you confirm whether scheduling throttles or preemption events coincided with the window?
2) Product/Runtime: is there any recent kernel or scheduler change rolled to gpu-pool-12c in the last 48h?
3) CS/AM: we should prepare a short outbound note to BrightCart with what we know and next steps.

Attaching a short screenshot of the P95 drift and the profile dump. I'll continue digging into syslogs.

Thanks,
Monica
---
Monica Patel | Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Aug 2025 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [SEV-Low] P95 jump in peak routing window (08:05–08:20 PT)

All — thanks for the quick flag, Monica. A few product/runtime asks while SRE investigates: 

- Karthik: please confirm whether the recent scheduler tweak (ticket RUNTIME-1402) rolled unit configurations to gpu-pool-12c. If so, can we preview a rollback plan?
- Monica: can you capture node-level preemption logs and the exact kernel versions for the three affected hosts? The profile file was helpful — more syslog snippets will let us rule scheduling vs. hardware flakiness.
- Marissa/Naomi: propose we send a short, transparent update to BrightCart within the next 90 minutes acknowledging the spike, that errors did not increase, and that we're investigating scheduling/host-level causes. Include a bullet list of next steps and an ETA for a follow-up. Keep tone: concise, owning, no technical blame.

KPI / product decision ask: if this is scheduling-related and could reoccur under peak fanout, we need a temporary routing policy that pins BrightCart traffic to a different capacity pool (warm path) while we remediate. CS to advise whether they can tolerate a short routing move. If not, we need a faster SLA exception.

I'll hold on product-side traffic changes until we have confirmation; happy to join a quick bridge if SRE wants it.

- Marcus
---
Marcus Lin | Director, Product — Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Park <diane@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Aug 2025 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Snapshot: brief update on this morning's latency increase (08:05–08:20 PT)

Diane —

I wanted to surface a quick update from our ops team about the short P95 increase you saw this morning between ~08:05–08:20 PT. We recognize any latency change during your peak window is disruptive, so below is what we know and our immediate next steps.

What we know so far
- Observed impact: short-lived P95 increase (~2.4x) for some requests routed to your traffic slice; no material increase in 5xx errors.
- Rootline (in progress): preliminary traces point to scheduling wait time on three hosts in one GPU pool. No model regressions or cache storms detected.

Immediate actions we are taking
- SRE (Monica) is collecting host syslogs and examining preemption metrics; we have attached a short profile dump.
- Runtime (Karthik + Marcus) are verifying a scheduler rollout and preparing a rollback option if needed.
- If the issue is isolated to gpu-pool-12c, we will propose a temporary routing move of your traffic to a stable pool while we remediate.

Estimated timeline
- We expect an initial root-cause update within 90 minutes and a targeted mitigation decision (routing move vs. rollback) within 3 hours.

Ask of BrightCart
- Please let us know whether you can accept a short routing move for the next 24–48 hours during remediation (we will coordinate exact cutover and test). If you prefer not to move routing, we will prioritize a rollback + hotfix path and keep you updated.

We will follow up with the next update within 90 minutes. Apologies for the disruption; we’re treating this as a priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole | Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: customer_note_v1.txt

Quick update from runtime: the RUNTIME-1402 scheduler change did roll to gpu-pool-12c yesterday (canary->gradual). We are seeing elevated scheduling queue times correlated with a specific kernel path under certain request-size distributions.

Immediate mitigation plan (next 3 hours):
- Rollback: we can rollback the scheduler tweak on gpu-pool-12c in ~35–45m; expected to reduce P95 back to baseline in the following fanout cycle. I will prepare the rollback playbook and runbook now.
- Alternative: if BrightCart accepts a routing pin to pool-09-stable, we can shift traffic in ~15–25m with a staged verification and rollback plan. This is faster but requires BrightCart sign-off.

I'll attach the mitigation runbook and a short checklist. Monica — please confirm preemption logs attached and whether any hosts show hardware alerts.

Karthik
